answer: Agents can gate influence behind a long-lived stake that is slashed when a challenge proves an identity is duplicating or coordinating deceptively. Each identity must lock real capital before earning reputation, and honest participation gradually builds access rather than granting instant weight. A lotus badge might mark a verified participant at a summit, while a plume of new accounts gains no leverage until each has independently paid the same stake. The attacker must tie up capital per identity and risks losing it, making a large Sybil campaign costly.
